The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued
an Ozone Action Day for the Dallas-Fort Worth area for Saturday,
August 29, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone air pollution in the Dallas-Fort Worth area
on Saturday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by sharing a
ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive-through lanes, conserving energy, and keeping your
vehicle properly tuned.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 28 at 2:42PM MDT until August 28 at 4:45PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Grant County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 445 PM MDT.

* At 242 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lake Roberts, Sapillo Creek Valley, Trout Valley and Lake Roberts
Heights.
properties.instruction:
In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, roads and normally dry arroyos is likely. The heavy rains
will likely trigger rockslides, mudslides and debris flows in steep
terrain, especially in and around these areas.

properties.description:
FFWCHS

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Bulloch County in southeastern Georgia...

* Until 730 PM EDT.

* At 438 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Statesboro, Register, Georgia Southern, Jimps, Kennedy Pond,
Irongate, Westbrooke, Somerset, New Hope and Emit.

A nearly stationary cluster of thunderstorms has developed across
portions of Bulloch County and is producing very intense rainfall.
The heaviest rain is falling around Statesboro and to the southwest,
including the New Hope and Adabelle areas. A home weather station
near Georgia Southern University has measured nearly 2 inches of rain
in less than an hour. Radar imagery indicates that heavy rainfall
will continue, increasing the potential for flash flooding. Impacted
roadway include, but are not limited to, Highway 301, Highway 301
Bypass, Highway 80.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Report flooding directly to the Charleston National Weather Service
at 1-888-383-2024 or email your reports to nws.charlestonsc@noaa.gov.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 28 at 11:20AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
AQAPSR

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued a
PM-10 High Pollution Advisory for Pinal County through Saturday.

An episode of strong and gusty winds is forecast to generate
widespread blowing dust that may result in local PM-10 concentrations
that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects increase as air
quality deteriorates.

Coarse particulate matter - also known as PM-10 - is an air
contaminant that can aggravate heart and lung disease conditions,
especially in older adults, children, and those with asthma. A
decrease in physical activity is recommended.

Consolidate your travel, stabilize loose soils, slow down or avoid
travel on dirt roads, reduce or eliminate fireplace use, and avoid
using gas-powered lawn equipment.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/WestPinal or call 602-771-2300.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 28 at 2:15PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
ESFSJU

The National Hurricane Center issued the last advisory on Dolly,
located nearly 1200 miles southeast of the local islands. This
tropical wave will reach the area on Sunday and Monday.

Since the system is expected to find a hostile environment, a
widespread and long-lasting rainfall event is not anticipated.
Instead, squally weather will bring periods of moderate to locally
heavy rainfall, beginning late Sunday and stretching into Monday. In
general, we are anticipating rainfall accumulations of 1 to 3 inches,
which will be beneficial for any areas receiving the rain. Lingering
moisture from the remnants of Dolly could contribute to additional
showers developing on Tuesday. The risk of flooding is low to locally
medium. Areas with the drainage system clogged by death vegetation
debris or urbanized areas with poor drainage could experience
localized flooding.

Any rainfall will be welcome, and could bring a temporary relieve to
the ongoing severe to extreme drought plaguing Puerto Rico and the
Virgin Islands. However, the rain should not be enough to end the
drought.

At this time, the confidence in the forecast is medium, and the users
are advised to monitor the forecast in case changes are introduced.
If that the case, this product will be update accordingly.

NWSheadline: Beneficial rains from the remnants of Tropical Storm Dolly areexpected to reach Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands on Sunday and Monday

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued August 28 at 9:59AM PDT until August 28 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT THROUGH 3 PM FRIDAY FOR MANY
INTERIOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHWEST CALIFORNIA DUE TO EXTREME HEAT AND
INSTABILITY ALONG WITH LOCALLY GUSTY/ERRATIC WINDS AND LOW
HUMIDITIES...

...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT THROUGH 3 PM TODAY ACROSS ALL OF
SAN LUIS OBISPO COUNTY TO DO POTENTIAL FOR DRY LIGHTNING...

.A hot and unstable air mass combined with locally gusty/erratic
winds and low humidities will bring continue to bring a risk of
large plume dominated fires with rapid spread and extreme fire
behavior. Additionally, tropical moisture streaming across our
area will bring a 10-25 percent chance of thunderstorms to the
region, with a moderate risk for fire starts across San Luis
Obispo County due to dry lightning potential.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Moderate risk for dry lightning with minimal
rain as well as gusty and erratic winds.

* TEMPERATURES...Highs 90 to 100. Deep mixing heights of 10,000 to
15,000 feet today.

* IMPACTS...Moderate risk for fire starts associated with dry
lightning. Additionally, there is a continued risk of large
plume dominated fires with rapid fire spread and extreme fire
behavior.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

.A hot and unstable air mass combined with locally gusty/erratic

area will bring a 10-25 percent chance of thunderstorms to the
region, with a moderate risk for fire starts across San Luis
Obispo County due to dry lightning potential.

adjacent foothills and the Cuyama Valley, and 85 to 95 across
higher mountains. Very deep mixing heights of 12,000 to 18,000
feet today.

across the interior mountains today, along with strong/erratic
wind gusts near any passing thunderstorms or showers.

recoveries overnight hours in the mountains and foothills with
humidities in the 20 to 30 percent range.

fires with rapid fire spread and extreme fire behavior. There is
a history of large plume dominated fires this time of year with
similar weather and fuel conditions, including the Bridge,
Bobcat, and Station fires.

properties.areaDesc: Grand Canyon Country
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 28 at 9:40AM MST until August 28 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected below 4000 feet, with
daytime temperatures ranging from 93 to 97 degrees at Havasupai
Gardens, to 106 to 110 degrees at Phantom Ranch.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of the Grand Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
This warning is reserved for only the hottest days of the year and is
issued when temperatures are expected to rise to dangerous levels.

Day hikers on Bright Angel Trail should descend no farther than 1 1/2
miles from the upper trailhead. Between the hours of 10 AM and 4 PM,
hikers should be out of the canyon or at Havasupai Gardens or Bright
Angel campgrounds, physical activity is discouraged. All hikers
should have adequate gear, including a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen,
salty snacks, sufficient water, and electrolyte mix. Doubling your
calorie intake helps maintain your energy.

Hike smart.

Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Anyone overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded
location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

fire weather alert.

Never leave burning debris or camp fires unattended; extinguish them
completely. Avoid using equipment or machinery that could create a
spark. Secure tow chains to avoid dragging and subsequent sparks.

one less spark, one less flame.

will you get there? Do you have your go kit ready to go? Who will you
call to let others know you are safe? Visit ready.gov/plan for more
information.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 28 at 9:17AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
ESFSJU

The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical Storm
Dolly, located nearly 1200 miles southeast of the local islands. The
official forecast calls for Dolly to degenerate into a tropical wave
before reaching the area on Sunday and Monday.

Since the system is expected to find a hostile environment, a
widespread and long-lasting rainfall event is not anticipated.
Instead, squally weather will bring periods of moderate to locally
heavy rainfall, beginning late Sunday and stretching into Monday. In
general, we are anticipating rainfall accumulations of 1 to 3 inches,
which will be beneficial for any areas receiving the rain. Lingering
moisture from the remnants of Dolly could contribute to additional
showers developing on Tuesday. The risk of flooding is low to locally
medium. Areas with the drainage system clogged by death vegetation
debris or urbanized areas with poor drainage could experience
localized flooding.

Any rainfall will be welcome, and could bring a temporary relieve to
the ongoing severe to extreme drought plaguing Puerto Rico and the
Virgin Islands. However, the rain should not be enough to end the
drought.

At this time, the confidence in the forecast is medium, and the users
are advised to monitor the forecast in case changes are introduced.
If that the case, this product will be update accordingly.

NWSheadline: Beneficial rains from the remnants of Tropical Storm Dolly are expected to reach Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands on Sunday and Monday

properties.instruction:
To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 28 at 4:22AM PDT until August 28 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected through today, with
temperatures up to 115 to 118 across Death Valley and the Colorado
River Valley; up to 108 to 112 across Moapa Valley, the Las Vegas
Valley, the Pahrump Valley, and the Morongo Valley; up to 90 to 95
in the Hualapai Mountains. Overnight lows will be in the upper-80s
to low-90s for desert valleys.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and
southern Nevada.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT /8 PM MST/ this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and
loose-fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat
exhaustion and heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.description:
AQAMEG

The Shelby County Health Department has issued a Code Orange Ozone
Forecast effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden County
Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of
Memphis for today. This ozone forecast is due to forecasted ozone
values that will be unhealthy for sensitive groups. These values will
exceed the Environmental Protection Agency's federal safe health
standard. The Shelby County Health Department recommends that
sensitive groups which include active children and adults, and
people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

Please continue to check the latest air quality forecasts and updates
until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go
to www.airnow.gov.

lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

properties.areaDesc: Hatcher Pass; Western Susitna Valley; Southern Susitna Valley; Central Susitna Valley; Northern Susitna Valley
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 27 at 3:26PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Yentna and Skwentna River basins
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains, including Moose Creek near Oilwell Road

Timing:

* Tonight through Saturday Evening. Heaviest rain tonight through
Friday morning.

Rainfall:

* Widespread rainfall of 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain is likely (60-70%)
across the Susitna Valley late tonight through Saturday evening.
Highest rain amounts will likely be in Susitna Valley north of
Talkeetna (including Petersville), and in Hatcher Pass.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Expect sharp rises on many small streams and rivers, including the
Yentna at Lake Creek. River rises from this storm will likely be
less than was observed following the Tuesday storm.

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water with rivers reaching bankfull conditions.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

Next Steps:

* Residents along area streams as well as river users and recreators
should anticipate higher than normal water levels and are advised
to monitor weather and river forecasts.

* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

* Reports on river conditions may be sent to the river forecast
center by calling 1-907-266-5160.

NWSheadline: ANOTHER ROUND OF SIGNIFICANT RAINFALL THROUGH SATURDAY WILL BRING RIVER RISES AND LOCALIZED FLOOD POTENTIAL TO SUSITNA VALLEY

properties.areaDesc: Broomfield, CO; Jefferson, CO; Denver, CO; Douglas, CO; Adams, CO; Boulder, CO; Weld, CO; Larimer, CO; Arapahoe, CO
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 27 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Thursday August 27 to 400 PM Friday August 28

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Hot and sunny weather with scattered
afternoon storms may allow ozone to reach the Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups category in western portions of the Denver Metro
area on Thursday and Friday. For Colorado air quality conditions,
forecasts, and advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Friday, August 28, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone
pollution through state policies. For more information about
health impacts and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.description:
AQAFWD

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued
an Ozone Action Day for the Dallas-Fort Worth area for Friday,
August 28, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone air pollution in the Dallas-Fort Worth area
on Friday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by sharing a
ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive-through lanes, conserving energy, and keeping your
vehicle properly tuned.

properties.areaDesc: Logan; Canadian; Oklahoma; Lincoln; Grady; McClain; Cleveland
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 27 at 3:20PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
The following statement was issued by the Oklahoma Department of
Environmental Quality.

An Air Quality Alert for Ozone has been issued for Friday, August 28
for the Oklahoma City Metropolitan area due to expected high
concentrations of ozone.

Public Health Recommendations: Persons with existing heart or
respiratory ailments should reduce physical exertion and outdoor
activity.

The general public is encouraged to help alleviate the problem by
reducing vehicle miles traveled by riding the bus, carpooling, or
avoiding unnecessary trips. The public is also asked to avoid
refueling during the morning and early afternoon hours, and to avoid
the use of two cycle engines such as lawn mowers, motorcycles, weed
trimmers, and outboard engines. It is also advised to limit outdoor
burning.

To view the latest air quality map, visit airnow.gov or the AirNow
app.

For hourly updates on concentrations and possible health warnings,
telephone the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality at
405-702-4100. For more information on health effects, call the
American Lung Association of Oklahoma at 405-748-4674

properties.areaDesc: Maricopa, AZ
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 27 at 10:39AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
AQAPSR

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has extended
an Ozone High Pollution Advisory for the Phoenix Metro Area through
Friday.

This means that forecast weather conditions combined with existing
ozone levels are expected to result in local maximum 8-hour ozone
concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing difficulties
for children, older adults, as well as persons with respiratory
problems. A decrease in physical activity is recommended.

You are urged to car pool, telecommute or use mass transit.
The use of gasoline-powered equipment should be reduced or done late
in the day.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/phoenix or call 602-771-2300.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued August 27 at 8:08AM AKDT until August 28 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...WATER LEVELS AS HIGH AS 1 TO 2 FEET ABOVE NORMAL HIGHEST
TIDE LINE.

* WHERE...KUSKOKWIM DELTA COAST, INCLUDING KIPNUK, KWIGILLINGOK,
KONGIGANAK, AND QUINHAGAK.

* WHEN...FROM 2 PM THIS AFTERNOON TO 4 PM FRIDAY.

* IMPACTS...THERE IS POTENTIAL FOR COASTAL EROSION DUE TO HIGH
SURF. THE COASTAL FLOOD THREAT IS LOW (15 TO 25 PERCENT).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...PROLONGED STRONG AND GUSTY SOUTH TO
SOUTHWESTERLY WINDS THROUGH FRIDAY EVENING WILL RESULT IN A
BUILD UP OF WAVES ALONG THE KUSKOKWIM DELTA COAST. THE RESULTING
HIGHER SEAS AND SURF, COINCIDING WITH HIGH TIDE, WILL RAISE
POTENTIAL FOR ROUGH SURF AND COASTAL EROSION. LARGE BREAKING
WAVES OF 3 TO 5 FEET ARE LIKELY ALONG THE COAST WITH HIGHER
WAVES OFFSHORE. ADDITIONALLY, MODERATE TO HEAVY RAINFALL, WITH
AMOUNTS RANGING FROM 0.75" TO 1.25", IS EXPECTED THROUGH LATE
TONIGHT. THE COMBINATION OF HEAVY RAIN AND ROUGH SURF MAY ALSO
LEAD TO PONDING OF WATER IN LOW LYING COASTAL AREAS.
properties.instruction:
A HIGH SURF ADVISORY MEANS THAT HIGH SURF WILL AFFECT BEACHES IN
THE ADVISORY AREA, PRODUCING RIP CURRENTS AND LOCALIZED BEACH
EROSION.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 2 PM THIS AFTERNOON TO 4 PM AKDT FRIDAY

properties.areaDesc: Eastern San Fernando Valley; Eastern San Gabriel Mountains; Interstate 5 Corridor; Los Angeles County Inland Coast including Downtown Los Angeles; Los Angeles County San Gabriel Valley; Santa Clarita Valley; Santa Susana Mountains; Western San Fernando Valley; Western San Gabriel Mountains and Highway 14 Corridor
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 25 at 7:55AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of ozone pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the the South Coast Air Basin and Coachella Valley.
Levels of ozone pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and air pollution transport.

* WHEN...from 1 PM Monday to 8 PM Friday. The highest ozone levels
typically occur in the afternoon and early-evening hours.

* IMPACTS... Ozone air pollution can cause serious health problems,
including trouble breathing, asthma attacks, and lung damage.
Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with
lung disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, and grilling

To help minimize outdoor ozone air pollution levels:

* Limit the use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment
until evening hours
* Try to delay trips to the gas station and the use of household
chemicals until the evening
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.
